test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A train covers a distance of 12 km in 25 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 5 km/hr, then the time (in minutes) taken by it to cover the same distance will be:
solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the train = 12 km.

Time taken = 25 minutes = 25/60 hours = 5/12 hours.

Initial speed = Distance / Time

Speed = 12 / (5/12) = 12 × 12 / 5 = 144 / 5 = 28.8 km/hr.

**Formula Used:**

New time taken = Distance / New speed

**Calculation:**

New speed = Initial speed - Decrease in speed

New speed = 28.8 km/hr - 5 km/hr = 23.8 km/hr

New time taken = Distance / New speed

New time taken = 12 km / 23.8 km/hr

New time taken in hours = 12 / 23.8

New time taken in hours = (12)/(23.8)

New time taken in hours = (6)/(11.9)

New time taken in minutes = (6)/(11.9) × 60

New time taken = 3600/119 = 30(30)/(119)

**The correct answer is option 2.**
